q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY)=(SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY)=(SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2), (3); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 1), (2, 2);
explanation: Q1 checks if the number of distinct products a customer has purchased is equal to the total number of distinct products in the database. Q2 checks if the concatenated string of distinct product keys a customer has purchased is the same as the concatenated string of all distinct product keys in the database.
counterexample_dsp: A customer has purchased all products, and another customer has purchased all products except for one. The first customer's concatenated product keys will match the database's concatenated product keys, but the second customer's will not.
